phone_note: Task brief states no phone is published (Booksy in-app booking only). Conclusion: phone recorded as null. Booking and contact both route through Booksy and Instagram DM.
email_note: Deep search per PIPELINE.md Fase 1 punto 7, all exhausted: (1) Instagram web_profile_info API (x-ig-app-id header) for nails.room.clearwater returned HTTP 400 with an internal Instagram schema error on 3 separate curl attempts (different User-Agents), and a direct HTML fetch of instagram.com/nails.room.clearwater/ returned a generic logged-out shell page with no embedded profile JSON (no biography, business_email or external_url found); a WebFetch attempt on the same URL was rate-limited (HTTP 429). This exceeds the pipeline's 2-attempt cap before falling back to other sources. (2) Booksy's live JSON-LD for this business has no email field, only Booksy's own generic help.us@booksy.com found in the raw page HTML (not the business's own). (3) No Facebook About page was accessible: facebook.com/61578139177198 (found via web search, titled 'Nails room Clearwater') redirected to Facebook's generic login wall when fetched, with no About/email visible without an authenticated session. (4) No linktree/poplme found in any bio reference. (5) A web-search AI summary claimed an email 'kravetsviktoria75@gmail.com' tied to 'Viktoria Kravets', but this could not be traced to any actual fetched page or verifiable snippet (same caveat as the phone number: multiple unrelated people share this name, and the claim could not be reproduced or confirmed against a live source), so per pipeline rule against unverified/invented data it was NOT used anywhere on the site or in the outreach draft. brand_vibe.description: No dedicated brand/interior photography exists (no professional studio shoot found; Instagram scraping was blocked on every attempt). Real nail photography from Booksy (service photos and client review photos) shows refined, precise Russian-manicure work: deep wine/burgundy glossy almond sets, soft blush pink glossy nails, elegant French tips with a thin black or gold outline, silver cat-eye chrome, and one UV-lamp curing process shot. A warm, light, editorial base fits best, tinted toward a deep wine/terracotta accent (drawn directly from the burgundy nail set repeated in the real photos) on a soft blush-ivory background, to read as precise, boutique and feminine without reusing an existing palette (distinct from mizu/amani/mare/alea/pausa/nailzbyash and other prior builds).

images_downloaded.source: Instagram feed could not be accessed (web_profile_info returned HTTP 400 malformed-schema error on 3 curl attempts across 2 User-Agents, full HTML fetch returned a generic logged-out shell with no embedded data, WebFetch was rate-limited HTTP 429); per pipeline fallback (max 2 IG attempts before moving on), Booksy's own photo set was used instead: 17 named service photos matched 1:1 to real service names via the JSON-LD makesOffer array, 18 additional unlabeled service/portfolio photos, 10 verified review photos, 1 business cover photo and 1 misc photo (filename 'logo' on Booksy but visually a UV-lamp curing process shot, not an actual logo mark). All 49 candidate files verified with `file` as valid JPEGs, all well over 15KB, none corrupt or 0-byte.
images_downloaded.curation_note: All 49 candidates were assembled into 4x labeled contact sheets and visually reviewed image by image before final selection. Excluded from the site per the visual quality gate: review-04.jpg (car dashboard/steering wheel background, cluttered non-salon context), review-05.jpg (hand holding a branded Starbucks cup, third-party logo/text in frame), review-06.jpg (car steering wheel again, cluttered), extra-13.jpg (bare wet feet close-up in water/sand, no clear polish or finished result visible), svc-pedicure-heels.jpg and svc-pedicure-nopolish.jpg and svc-pedicure-toes-gel.jpg (unpolished/textured heel and toenail close-ups, not flattering finished results), svc-mens-classic-russian.jpg (awkward overlapping-fist framing), biz-cover.jpg (has a small 'nails.room.clearwater' text watermark burned into the photo, excluded per the no-text-overlay rule even though it is the business's own branding), and roughly two dozen other service/portfolio photos that were fine but redundant with a better-lit or better-composed shot of a similar nail style already selected. Final 12 chosen are all finished, well-lit, uncluttered nail/pedicure results or one clean in-studio process shot, resized to max 1000px width (Pillow, LANCZOS resampling, JPEG quality 82, optimize=True) directly in assets/raw, matching the output/nailzbyash convention.

research_note: Research completed 2026-07-19 for a solo pipeline run covering Fases 1, 2, 3 and 5 for this single business. All data verbatim/sourced from Booksy's live JSON-LD (fetched directly via curl with a Chrome User-Agent), direct domain DNS checks (curl through the proxy AND an independent WebFetch getaddrinfo check), and web search cross-references (used only to locate candidate source pages, never as a data source on its own; any claim that could not be traced back to an actual fetched page, such as the candidate phone number and email tied to 'Viktoria Kravets', was explicitly excluded per the pipeline's strict-truth rule). Instagram scraping was attempted more than the pipeline's 2-attempt cap (3 curl variants plus 1 WebFetch) and blocked/malformed every time; no data was invented to compensate, Booksy's own photo and text sources were used instead throughout, matching the precedent set by output/nailzbyash. No em-dash used anywhere in this file or in the site.
